prompt:
Q: Given an undirected graph with n vertices, no matter how you complete DFS, I can always complete
BFS in the same order. What can you say about this graph?
judge_reasoning: Candidate [1] claims the graph must be a path, which is the most plausible characterization among the options given the strong requirement that BFS can match any DFS completion order. Candidate [3] and [4] are too general (“tree”), since many trees admit DFS orders that BFS cannot reproduce due to BFS’s level/queue constraints. Candidate [2] (“complete graph”) is not supported and is very unlikely to satisfy the stated “no matter how DFS is completed” condition. Overall, [1] best matches the expected structural restriction.
